title: Three Uncapped Players, Three Different Roads. Before Dharamsala, Meet the Men Who Could Debut on Saturday.
excerpt: Prince Yadav bowled Kohli in the IPL. Gurnoor Brar is six-foot-five and generates fear. Harsh Dubey broke a 46-year Ranji record. All three are in India's ODI squad for a historic first bilateral series against Afghanistan.
body:
When India walk out at Dharamsala on Saturday for the first ODI against Afghanistan, the team sheet will carry three names that have never appeared on an international scorecard. Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar, and Harsh Dubey are not here because the selectors ran out of options. They are here because each of them did something in the last twelve months that made it impossible to ignore them any longer.

This is also, quietly, a historic series. India and Afghanistan have never played a bilateral ODI series before. They have met in World Cups and Asia Cups, and India demolished Afghanistan by an innings and 300 runs in the one-off Test last week. But three ODIs across Dharamsala, Lucknow, and Chennai — June 13, 17, and 20 — mark the first time the two nations will contest a standalone one-day series on Indian soil.

With Virat Kohli ruled out after tearing his hamstring in the IPL final, Jasprit Bumrah rested, and Mohammad Siraj not in the squad, there is genuine room in this eleven for new faces. Captain Shubman Gill has fifteen players to choose from. At least one of the three uncapped men is almost certain to play.

## Prince Yadav: The IPL Breakout Who Bowled Kohli

Prince Yadav is twenty-four years old, from Delhi, and until eighteen months ago he was best known as a net bowler for Lucknow Super Giants. That changed in IPL 2026, when he took 16 wickets in 14 matches at an economy of 8.83, operating primarily in the powerplay and at the death.

The wicket that turned heads came against Royal Challengers Bengaluru: Yadav bowled Kohli with an in-swinging delivery that held its line and clipped the top of off stump. It was not a fluke. Yadav's defining strength is his ability to hit a nagging length and extract lateral movement, the kind of bowling that is hardest to score off in 50-over cricket.

In List A cricket, he has 29 wickets in 14 matches. He was serving as a net bowler for the Test squad in Mullanpur before being told to shift to the ODI camp. The transformation from nets to squad in the span of a single IPL season is the kind of story Indian cricket produces once every few years. For NRIs who watched the IPL and remember the Kohli dismissal, Prince Yadav is already a familiar name. Saturday could make it official.

## Gurnoor Brar: The Tall Man from Muktsar

Gurnoor Brar is six feet four-and-a-half inches tall. He bowls right-arm fast. He is from Muktsar, a small city in southern Punjab, and he started his professional career as a net bowler for Mumbai Indians during the 2019 IPL. He was nineteen.

Seven years later, he is in both the Test and ODI squads for the Afghanistan series. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar has said publicly that Brar is on the radar for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.

The numbers back the noise. In the 2024-25 Ranji Trophy, Brar was Punjab's leading wicket-taker with 26 wickets in seven matches. In the Sher-E-Punjab T20, he topped the wicket-takers' chart with 22 wickets in 11 matches at an average of 14. In first-class cricket overall, he has 52 wickets in 18 matches with a best of 5/14.

What separates Brar from other tall Indian quicks is not just bounce — it is the ability to generate steep, uncomfortable bounce on surfaces that offer nothing to other bowlers. Modern coaches call it hitting the hard length. For the massive Punjabi diaspora watching from Surrey, Brampton, and Fremont, a debut at Dharamsala from a Muktsar boy would be personal.

## Harsh Dubey: The Record-Breaker Ashwin Mentored

Harsh Dubey is twenty-three, a left-arm orthodox spinner from Vidarbha, and he holds the record for the most wickets in a single Ranji Trophy season — 69, surpassing Bihar's Ashutosh Aman (68, set in 2018-19) and Bishan Singh Bedi's 64 from 1974-75.

Those 69 wickets came alongside 476 runs with the bat. He was named Player of the Tournament as Vidarbha won the 2024-25 Ranji Trophy. In the quarter-final against Tamil Nadu, he scored half-centuries in both innings and took four wickets. In the final against Kerala, his three-wicket haul in the first innings gave Vidarbha the lead they never surrendered.

What makes Dubey's story richer is his mentor. For the past four years, he has spent his off-seasons in Chennai playing league cricket for the Mylapore Recreational Club under the guidance of Ravichandran Ashwin — the same Ashwin who, just last week, praised Gill's captaincy evolution during the Afghanistan Test. Ashwin's fingerprints are on Dubey's craft: the patience, the ability to extract turn from unhelpful surfaces, the discipline to bowl long spells without losing control.

In the IPL, Dubey plays for Sunrisers Hyderabad. In first-class cricket, he has 133 wickets in 27 matches at an average of 23.26 with nine five-wicket hauls. He is, by any measure, the most accomplished red-ball cricketer in this squad who has not yet played for India.

## What It Means for the 2027 World Cup Cycle

For Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, the Afghanistan ODI series matters less for its results — India are overwhelming favourites — and more for what it reveals about the next cycle. The 2027 World Cup in South Africa is fifteen months away. Rohit Sharma, who cleared his fitness test at the BCCI Centre of Excellence earlier this week, is thirty-nine. Hardik Pandya, also cleared, has been managing his body for years. Kohli is injured.

The question is not whether India's old guard can win three ODIs against Afghanistan. It is whether the next generation — the Prince Yadavs, the Gurnoor Brars, the Harsh Dubeys — can take their chance when the stage is smaller and the stakes feel low, and then hold their place when the stage gets bigger.

Gambhir's India has been aggressive about blooding new talent. Manav Suthar debuted in the Test last week and broke a 46-year record. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who is fifteen, is with the India A squad. The pipeline is producing. Dharamsala on Saturday will tell us whether it is producing fast enough.
